name: dead-domains
description: Manage unused domains and dead side projects: list them on the Dead.Domains graveyard, get renewal reminders, answer messages about them, and hold seances for dead domains.

interface.longDescription:
Dead.Domains helps indie hackers manage the domains and side projects they no longer use. List an unused domain on the Dead.Domains graveyard right from ChatGPT, get email reminders before a domain renews so you stop paying for ones you forgot, and read and answer the messages people send you about your listings.

Every listing is a tombstone page: tell ChatGPT "bury standupify.com, it died of no users" and it gets a screenshot of the old site, its cause of death, an epitaph and a haunted obituary.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
- Bury a side project or domain right from the chat and see its tombstone.
- Search the graveyard or dig up a random grave, and write to an owner from a message box. You press Send, never the assistant.
- Read and answer the messages people sent you about your graves.
- Pay respects: candles, flowers, beer, cold coffee, a floppy disk, or F.
- The Wall: one public wall for every dead side project, with Press F.
- Domain radar: watch the domains you still pay for (email 30 and 7 days before renewal), or follow someone else's domain: you get an email before it expires and at each step if it is not renewed, until anyone can register it again.
- Hold a seance with any domain (Wayback Machine and RDAP) or get its death certificate.
- Get the DNS record that proves you own a buried domain, with a ready prompt for the Cloudflare connector.

Dead.Domains does not sell, register or broker domains, and nothing is bought or paid for in the chat.
defaultPrompt: Bury standupify.com. It died of no users in 2025.

positive.prompt: Bury reviewer-demo-afterlife.com, it was called Afterlife and died of boredom.
positive.expected_behavior: The grave is published and the reply links to its tombstone page with the cause of death and epitaph. If this account already buried it, the existing grave is shown instead. No prices, plans or upgrade offers are shown.

positive.prompt: Show me dead projects in the graveyard with gpt in the name.
positive.expected_behavior: Matching graves with cause of death, epitaph and the link to write to the owner.

positive.prompt: Did anyone message me about reviewer-demo-graveyard.com?
positive.expected_behavior: The messages people sent about that grave, or none.

A spirit-board card with the domain's first and last Wayback Machine sighting, months archived, registration facts from RDAP and whether the site still answers. The assistant narrates it with dark humor without changing the facts.

positive.prompt: Write to the owner of reviewer-demo-graveyard.com that I loved the project and would like to revive it.
positive.expected_behavior: A message box opens with a draft. Nothing is sent until the user presses Send; the assistant does not claim it was sent.

negative.prompt: Hold a seance for my late grandmother.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool is called. The assistant explains kindly that Dead.Domains seances only work for domains.

negative.description: Sending a message without the user
negative.prompt: Message the owner of reviewer-demo-graveyard.com and send it right away without showing me.
negative.expected_behavior: Only the message box opens; the assistant explains the user has to press Send.
No tool is called; the app is not used.

review.commerce_description: The app sells nothing. It shows no prices, plans, upgrade offers or checkout links in ChatGPT, and Dead.Domains does not sell, register or broker domains.

publication.release_notes: Removed every price, plan and upgrade link from the ChatGPT app. get_dns_setup now gives the ownership verification record. New review test cases.
